Resolves #20192

The grid post said "If the App Worker spends 300 ms sorting, nothing on the main thread waits for it." That number was never measured, and readers took it as the grid's cost to sort. The sentence now states the mechanism: "However long the App Worker spends sorting, nothing on the main thread waits for it." The rest of the paragraph and the rest of the post are unchanged.

Evidence: L1 (docs; one sentence, every other figure in the post audited against the source it links) → L1 required (no runtime ACs). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the baseline `pr-body` and `substrate-size` checks run in CI. Change class: zero-delta (`docs`).

Micro-review eligible: docs — one sentence of prose, no code, no registry change.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | Line 54 states the mechanism and carries no number. After the change, `grep -c "300 ms"` on the post returns 0 |
| AC-2 | Every line of the post holding a digit was read (`grep -n "[0-9]"`, 40 lines). Each timing sits in a sentence that links its source: the benchmark report at `4300c48` (lines 15, 76–94) and the 10.5 release notes (line 63). The 60 Hz frame budget and the 50 ms long task link MDN (line 21). The pool and DOM counts were read at source or measured on the production bigData example (lines 60–66; method in PR `#20186`'s Test Evidence). DevIndex's sizes come from its repository (lines 9, 98–104). The other figures are dates, versions, scenario sizes, or line 39's "move this row down 500 pixels", which shows the shape of a change message and puts no cost on Neo.mjs. No other cost of Neo.mjs is unsourced |
| AC-3 | Post-merge: see Post-Merge Validation |

None substantive.
